title: AI Unlocked: NGOs & Nonprofits
blurb: For NGO leaders and program staff: grant-winning proposal engines, donor reporting on autopilot, M&E acceleration, low-bandwidth field workflows, and safeguarding-aware data ethics — built by a practitioner who has strengthened NGO systems on three continents.

modules.d: Doing more mission with the same grant — where AI moves the needle.
modules.body:
The math of leverage

NGOs run on scarce unrestricted funds. AI attacks the overhead line directly: proposals, reports, translations, and admin that consumed staff-weeks now take days. That difference is programming money.

  • Map your organization's document lifecycle: proposal → workplan → M&E → donor report. Every arrow is an AI acceleration point.
  • The plAIbox NGO you built in Level 1 becomes real methodology here.
The UN’s AI for Good platform (ITU) exists on a simple thesis: AI’s highest return is on the Sustainable Development Goals — health, education, hunger, dignity. NGOs are the delivery mechanism of that thesis. Every hour this course returns to your mission is the thesis proven.

modules.d: From call-for-proposals to submission-ready draft in days.
modules.body:
Workflows

  • RFP decoder: paste the call → eligibility checklist, evaluation criteria weights, and a compliance matrix.
  • Logframe builder: goal → outcomes → outputs → indicators drafted, then your field reality pass.
  • Boilerplate bank: capability statements, past performance, org profiles maintained as reusable, versioned assets.
  • Donor-voice tuning: the same project narrated for USAID-style, EU-style, and foundation-style reviewers.
plAIbox™: take a real open call and produce the compliance matrix, logframe, and 5-page narrative draft — mentor plays donor reviewer.
🧪 Interactive Lab — try it now

Act as a proposal strategist. Here is a funding call: [paste]. Produce a compliance matrix (every requirement, where we’ll address it), a draft logframe (goal, 2 outcomes, 4 outputs, indicators), and a 400-word concept note in the donor’s voice — then list the five weakest points a reviewer would attack.

quiz.q: The first artifact to build from any call for proposals is…
opts: A compliance matrix from the call itself

modules.d: Grant tools, Google for Nonprofits, Canva NP, and CRM AI compared — with free-tier access paths.
modules.body:
Comparative snapshot

  • Google Workspace for Nonprofits: free tier with Gemini features arriving — the backbone.
  • Canva for Nonprofits: free Pro-class design for eligible orgs — apply with registration docs.
  • Grant discovery/writing tools (Instrumentl-class, Grantable-class): subscriptions; test in trial windows against a real deadline.
  • General LLMs + NotebookLM: your proposal and reporting engine; NotebookLM turns project docs into briefings and even audio updates for field teams.
  • Make/Zapier: beneficiary-form intake, donor thank-yous, and report data collection automated.

modules.d: From field data to donor-ready reports without the all-nighters.
modules.body:
Workflows

  • Indicator tracking sheets AI-summarized into narrative progress against logframe targets.
  • Beneficiary story drafting from field notes — with consent and dignity standards enforced.
  • Variance explanations and risk registers drafted for review, not invention: numbers come from your data only.
  • Multi-donor reporting: one master report transformed to each donor's template.

modules.d: Low-bandwidth workflows and safeguarding-grade data discipline.
modules.body:
Field-first design

  • Offline-capable and WhatsApp-based collection; batch AI processing when connectivity returns.
  • Local-language translation workflows with human verification for sensitive content.

Hard lines

  • Beneficiary PII, protection cases, and safeguarding data never enter consumer AI tools.
  • Consent, dignity, and do-no-harm review for any AI-generated imagery or stories of beneficiaries.

opts: In any AI tool that helps
Only in approved systems — never consumer AI

modules.body:
Capstone

  • Your proposal engine assets, one automated reporting workflow, the tool matrix with eligibility/free-tier notes, and a 2-page organizational AI policy (data classes, approvals, disclosure) — presented as if to your board.
